chunks: From him, from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī, from Aban, from Isma'il al-Ju'fi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A camel falls into a well, how is it slaughtered? He said: 'Insert the spear and stab it with it, say the name [of God], and eat [its meat].'

key_terms.وَيُسَمِّي: And he says the name [of God]

ai.seo_question: How to slaughter a trapped animal like a camel in a well according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *dham al-sabil* (ease in difficulty) by permitting the slaughter of a trapped camel via piercing with a spear (*harba*) rather than the standard throat-cutting method. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes that as long as the slaughterer recites the name of God (*tasmiya*) at the moment of killing, the meat remains *halal*, highlighting the flexibility of Shia fiqh in handling unique practical scenarios.
